4. // PhysicalAddress — Specifications
5. //
6. // A `PhysicalAddress` abstracts to a single mathematical integer: the raw
7. // physical address (`PhysicalAddress@ : int`, defined by the `View` impl in
8. // `phys.rs`, delegating to the inner `VirtualAddress`). The only derived notion
9. // callers reason about is the *frame* the address lies in
10. // (`addr / FRAME_SIZE == addr >> FRAME_SHIFT`), used to index the frame
11. // allocator's bitmaps / refcount arrays.
12. //
13. // Trust-boundary helpers pin the not-yet-verified `arch` `FrameNumber` type and
14. // the `arch`/`sys` library-edge constants/methods this module calls. They mirror
15. // the existing `sys`/`arch` `assume_specification` boundaries the codebase
16. // already draws (`::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` in `frame.rs`, the `Address` trait
17. // methods in `page.spec.rs` / `kframe.spec.rs`). `spec_page_size()` is the
18. // canonical frame size, re-exported from `crate::hal::mem` (defined alongside
19. // `FrameAddress`); `FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE == spec_page_size()`.
20. 
21. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
22. verus! {
23. 
24. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
25. use vstd::arithmetic::power2::pow2;
26. use vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::{
27.     lemma_fundamental_div_mod,
28.     lemma_mod_division_less_than_divisor,
29.     lemma_div_by_multiple,
30.     lemma_mod_multiples_basic,
31. };
32. use vstd::bits::lemma_usize_shr_is_div;
33. 
34. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
35. // `View`/datatype registration reachable here. Declare it to Verus as an opaque
36. // external datatype so it may appear in spec-fn parameters and the
37. // `assume_specification`s below. Its internals are not modeled (`external_body`):
38. // its abstract index is projected by `spec_frame_raw_value`.
39. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
40. #[verifier::external_body]
41. pub struct ExFrameNumber(FrameNumber);
42. 
43. // ── Frame-number trust-boundary projections (arch `FrameNumber`) ──────────────
44. //
45. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
46. // `View` impl reachable here (orphan rule). Its abstract index is therefore
47. // projected by an uninterpreted ghost function, exactly as `view_design.md`
48. // prescribes. `spec_max_frame_number()` denotes `FrameNumber::MAX`.
49. 
50. // The integer index of a frame number (`0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`).
51. pub uninterp spec fn spec_frame_raw_value(frame: FrameNumber) -> int;
52. 
53. // The largest representable frame number. Mirrors `arch FrameNumber::MAX ==
54. // MAX_ADDRESS / FRAME_SIZE - 1 == usize::MAX / FRAME_SIZE - 1`. Interpreting it
55. // against `usize::MAX` and `spec_page_size()` is what lets verified constructors
56. // discharge their `usize` multiply (no-overflow) obligation: a frame index in
57. // `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()` scaled by `spec_page_size()` stays `<= usize::MAX`.
58. pub open spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int {
59.     usize::MAX as int / spec_page_size() - 1
60. }
61. 
62. // ── Derived spec helpers over the View domain (`int`) ─────────────────────────
63. 
64. // The frame an address lies in: exact integer division, independent of whether
65. // the implementation shifts (`>> FRAME_SHIFT`) or divides (`/ FRAME_SIZE`).
66. pub open spec fn spec_frame_number(addr_view: int) -> int {
67.     addr_view / spec_page_size()
68. }
69. 
70. // The base (frame-aligned) address of a frame index: `frame * FRAME_SIZE`.
71. pub open spec fn spec_from_number(frame_view: int) -> int {
72.     frame_view * spec_page_size()
73. }
74. 
75. // ── `arch`/`sys` library-edge `assume_specification`s ─────────────────────────
76. 
77. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE` is the frame size (alias of `PAGE_SIZE`), tied to the
78. // canonical `spec_page_size()`. It is strictly positive (`== 4096`); positivity is
79. // the load-bearing fact for the division/modulo reasoning in the constructors.
80. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE ] -> (result: usize)
81.     ensures
82.         result == spec_page_size(),
83.         spec_page_size() > 0,
84. ;
85. 
86. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT == log2(FRAME_SIZE)`. Bounded below the pointer width
87. // so `raw_addr >> FRAME_SHIFT` is well-defined, and `2^FRAME_SHIFT == FRAME_SIZE`
88. // so the shift coincides with division by `spec_page_size()`.
89. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT ] -> (result: usize)
90.     ensures
91.         result < usize::BITS,
92.         pow2(result as nat) == spec_page_size(),
93. ;
94. 
95. // `VirtualAddress::new` is a pure newtype constructor: the wrapped value is the
96. // abstract address. (`sys` library edge; the inner module is not yet verified.)
97. pub assume_specification[ VirtualAddress::new ](value: usize) -> (result: VirtualAddress)
98.     ensures
99.         result@ == value as int,
100. ;
101. 
102. // `<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value` is pure newtype identity: the
103. // returned raw `usize` equals the abstract address.
104. pub assume_specification[ <VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value ](
105.     addr: VirtualAddress,
106. ) -> (result: usize)
107.     ensures
108.         result as int == addr@,
109. ;
110. 
111. // `FrameNumber::into_raw_value` projects a frame number to its index; every
112. // `FrameNumber` value is in range (`0 ..= MAX`) by construction.
113. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::into_raw_value ](frame: FrameNumber) -> (result: usize)
114.     ensures
115.         result as int == spec_frame_raw_value(frame),
116.         0 <= spec_frame_raw_value(frame) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
117. ;
118. 
119. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value` succeeds iff `value <= MAX`, preserving the index.
120. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::from_raw_value ](value: usize) -> (result: Option<FrameNumber>)
121.     ensures
122.         match result {
123.             Some(f) => value as int <= spec_max_frame_number()
124.                 && spec_frame_raw_value(f) == value as int,
125.             None => value as int > spec_max_frame_number(),
126.         },
127. ;
128. 
129. // ── Type invariant ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130. //
131. // Every `PhysicalAddress` a verified constructor produces has a *representable
132. // frame number*: `self@ / FRAME_SIZE <= FrameNumber::MAX`. This is the load-
133. // bearing fact that makes `into_frame_number` total (its internal
134. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never panics), which the frame
135. // allocator relies on when using the result directly as a bitmap / refcount
136. // index. It is *not* alignment (MMIO addresses may be unaligned) and *not*
137. // RAM-validity (`from_mmio_address` deliberately bypasses that check).
138. impl PhysicalAddress {
139.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
140.         spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
141.     }
142. }
